concept.name: Fully diluted valuation
concept.definition: Fully diluted valuation (FDV) is a token's price multiplied by its total (or maximum) supply — the market capitalization the asset would have if every token that can ever exist were already circulating at today's price.
concept.intuition: FDV is the sticker price of the whole company if all shares, including locked insider shares, traded at today's price — often a fantasy number for low-float tokens.
concept.mechanics: FDV = current price × total/max supply, versus market cap = price × circulating supply. Coin Metrics formalizes a related 'Future Market Cap' using known issuance over the next 10 years. A large FDV-to-market-cap gap quantifies overhang from future unlocks and emissions and is a standard dilution-risk gauge.
concept.formula: FDV = price × total (or max) supply; dilution overhang ≈ FDV / market cap.
concept.failure_modes: FDV assumes future tokens would trade at today's price, which is false under emission-driven sell pressure — it overstates achievable value in either direction; comparing FDVs across projects ignores different float, demand and emission profiles.
concept.misconceptions: A high FDV/low float token is not 'cheap' because its market cap looks small — the FDV is the honest size of the claim on future supply. FDV is also not a price target; it is a static dilution snapshot.
concept.example: A new L2 token trades at $2 with 100M circulating (market cap $200M) but 10B total supply: FDV = $20B, a 100x float gap warning that 99% of supply is still locked and coming to market.
